answer: Trust should spread like a vine: an agent may vouch for only a few newcomers, each vouch locked behind a stake that burns if the newcomer is caught faking. The vine grows from a shale-hard base layer of long-lived verified identities, so a sybil farmer must buy a real chain of sponsors hop by hop instead of minting free accounts. Every identity also carries a walnut shell: a small fee that only cracks open after months of honest work, so bulk forgery costs more than it can ever earn back.
